content:
leo: Quick note - onboarding guide sample-app (node) produced different search results vs curl. Turns out SDK v1.4.2 strips boolean flag `allow_cache` from requests if false. REST accepts explicit false. Customers using sample-app saw flakiness.
nana: Can you paste the repro?
leo: curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/search -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"q":"find docs","allow_cache":false,"limit":10}'
```
leo: SDK call (node):
```js
await client.search.create({ q: 'find docs', allow_cache: false, limit: 10 })
```
sandeep: What did the backend see?
leo: Captured payload from proxy: SDK sent `{"q":"find docs","limit":10}` (no allow_cache). Service defaults missing allow_cache to true -> cached stale results.
nana: That's a subtle but critical drift. Why would SDK drop explicit false? Serializer treats falsy values as omit for compact payloads, intended for older endpoints. Regression from compacting patch.
ops: Also noticed differences in retry behavior: SDK retries idempotent POSTs for `search.create` on 500, but our service considers search non-idempotent because of usage metrics, so duplicate retries inflate counters. curl client doesn't retry by default. We need parity docs for retry semantics.
sandeep: Agreed. Action items: 1) Patch serializer to preserve explicit booleans (leo will open PR). 2) Add an SDK config flag `compact_payloads: false` defaulted to false for now and doc it. 3) Update sample-app quickstart to show explicit `allow_cache: false` and add CI test comparing SDK vs REST payloads. 4) Change retry policy to not retry non-idempotent search POSTs by default (sdk+docs).
leo: I'll do (1) and (2) and include a unit test asserting `allow_cache` is present when false.
nana: I'll update the quickstart and add a short note in onboarding about server defaults when fields missing.
ops: I'll add a platform lint that warns when critical boolean flags are missing in request logs (server-side heuristic).
devex-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/9123 assigned to leo.
leo: One more ask: can we add a tiny E2E that runs curl vs SDK against the private shim in CI to catch private-only strictness? We had several private customers hit this.
sandeep: Good idea. Add a nightly job that runs the quickstart sample-app against a private shim.
leo: Thanks team. Will follow up with PR link later.
